name: SUDAN
lead: Sudan is in northeast Africa, where Africa meets the Arab world. Two great Nile rivers meet at its capital, Khartoum. Desert covers the north. Long ago, a Sudanese kingdom ruled all of Egypt.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Desert covers northern Sudan, including the Nubian Desert. The Nile winds through the country. Its Blue and White branches meet at Khartoum.
In the west, Jebel Marra, a sleeping volcano, rises nearly 3,000 m. A sparkling lake fills its crater. The south is green and swampy. The east meets the Red Sea.
animals: The Nile crocodile grows up to 5 metres long. It waits for hours without moving. Dorcas gazelles dart across the northern desert and get water from plants.
Dromedary camels have crossed the Nubian Desert for thousands of years. Lions and leopards hunt in the south. The African rock python is Africa's longest snake.
culture: Sudanese hosts offer guests strong spiced coffee or sweet tea. Nubian people paint bold geometric patterns on walls and play drums and the oud, a lute.
Weddings last several nights, with henna patterns on hands and feet. The giant Omdurman souq (market) sells spices and gold jewellery. Ful medames, spiced beans, is the favourite breakfast.
history: About 2,600 years ago, the Kingdom of Kush grew powerful. Its rulers, the Black Pharaohs, conquered all of Egypt. Kushite kings built hundreds of steep pyramids along the Nile.
Sudan won independence in 1956 after Ottoman and British-Egyptian rule. In 2011, South Sudan voted to separate. It became Africa's newest nation, peacefully.
wows: Sudan has more ancient pyramids than Egypt, over 200 at Meroë alone.
The Black Pharaohs of Kush conquered Egypt in 747 BC and ruled for nearly a century.
At Khartoum, a blue-green river and a muddy-brown river flow side by side.
Jebel Marra erupted just 3,500 years ago, and its crater lake has hot springs.
Sudan's pyramids are steeper than Egypt's: 72 degrees, not 54.
Omdurman has Africa's largest camel market.
Egypt called this land Nubia, from its word for gold.

myths.fact: Rivers flow downhill, in any direction. The Nile runs north to the Mediterranean Sea.

myths.myth: The Sahara is the world's biggest desert
myths.fact: Antarctica is bigger. A desert is any place with very little rain, hot or cold.
